section_summary: This section covers internal political and administrative developments in Japan between August 1934 and May 1935, beginning with the fall of the Saito Cabinet following the Teijin financial scandal and the accession of Admiral Keisuke Okada as Prime Minister. The documents detail the Okada Cabinet's composition and policy platform, the impending expiration of the Washington Naval Treaty and demands for naval parity, and intense inter-ministerial struggles among the Army, Foreign Office, and Overseas Ministry regarding administrative reforms in Manchukuo and the Kwantung Leased Territory. Additionally, the section traces the vehement resistance of Kwantung civilian police to gendarmerie oversight, cabinet personnel changes including Takahashi succeeding Fujii as Finance Minister and Minami replacing Hishikari in Manchuria, and the establishment of the Cabinet Deliberative Body and Cabinet Investigation Bureau.

subfiles.about: Analysis of the formation of the Okada Cabinet following the collapse of the Saito Cabinet and its implications for Japan's naval policy and forthcoming disarmament conferences.
subfiles.summary: Discusses the resignation of Premier Saito and Finance Minister Takahashi triggered by financial scandals involving Vice-Minister Kuroda and other officials. Explains the selection of Admiral Keisuke Okada as a moderate compromise candidate acceptable to the Emperor's liberal advisers while placating the Navy. Details the balance of power between moderates seeking peaceful international relations and military extremists demanding abrogation of naval treaties and parity.
subfiles.title: Japan: The New Okada Cabinet and Japan's Naval Program

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 918 (Political Report No. 80) regarding the resignation of the Saito Cabinet and formation of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 918 (Political Report No. 80), dated August 4, 1934, regarding the resignation of the Saito Cabinet and the installation of the new ministry under Admiral Keisuke Okada. Indicates the primary document is filed under 894.00 P.R./80.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.00 P.R./80 (Despatch No. 918)

subfiles.about: Detailed monthly report on Japanese internal political affairs, party alignments, government policy statements, army programs, and military movements during July 1934.
subfiles.summary: Presents Section III (Internal Political Affairs) of the Embassy's monthly report for July 1934. Details the composition of the Okada Cabinet, the text and press reception of its ten-point policy platform, and the political friction between the supporting Minseito and the alienated Seiyukai. Also covers the arrest of the East Asia Supremacy Society plotters, the War Ministry's defense platform and budget proposals, high-level military personnel shifts, and air defense drills in Osaka.
subfiles.title: Internal Political Affairs (Japan Monthly Political Report for July 1934)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 918 enclosing the statement of policy of the new Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 918, dated August 3, 1934, which encloses and comments upon the official policy statement issued by the newly formed Okada Cabinet. Filed under 894.00/534 with decimal cross-reference 894.002/250.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/250 (Despatch No. 918)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 943 regarding Cabinet disputes over the administration of Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Embassy Despatch No. 943 regarding the proposal to centralize Japanese administration in Manchuria under the Ambassador and Kwantung Army Commander. Highlights the Foreign Office's opposition to proposals that would undermine claims of Manchukuo's sovereign independence. Notes the reported compromise to abolish the Governor of Kwantung and replace him with a Secretary-General to the Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 943

subfiles.about: Embassy report on the fierce inter-departmental struggle among the War, Foreign, and Overseas Ministries over unified administrative control in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Reports on the deep rift within the Japanese Cabinet concerning representation in Manchukuo and control of the Kwantung Leased Territory and South Manchuria Railway. Analyzes the conflicting stances: the War Office demanding supreme administrative power under the Prime Minister, the Foreign Office defending diplomatic integrity and Manchukuo's sovereignty, and the Overseas Ministry resisting the loss of colonial authority. Notes the threat of mass resignation from civil officials of the Kwantung Government.
subfiles.title: Japanese Cabinet Ministers Disagree Over Control of Representation in Manchuria (Despatch No. 943)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzing Tokyo Despatch No. 1005 on the Cabinet agreement regarding the reorganization of Manchurian administrative organs.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes the Cabinet's agreement to reorganize administration in Manchuria into a dual system headed by the Ambassador concurrently serving as Commander-in-Chief of the Kwantung Army. Highlights the creation of a Manchurian Affairs Bureau in Tokyo directly responsible to the Prime Minister. Observes that the outcome represents a decisive victory for the Army and demonstrates its absolute control over policy in Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1005

subfiles.about: Embassy report detailing the Cabinet's compromise plan centralizing administrative control in Manchuria under military authority.
subfiles.summary: Transmits details of the unanimous Cabinet decision adopting Premier Okada's compromise plan for Manchurian administration, largely capitulating to War Ministry demands. Explains the structural changes: unifying the Ambassadorship and Kwantung Army command, establishing a Manchurian Affairs Bureau headed by War Minister Hayashi, and subordinating civilian police to the Gendarmerie commander. Reports intense resistance, including threats of mass resignation and an outbreak of violence among civilian police officers.
subfiles.title: Japanese Representation in Manchuria to Remain under Control of Military (Despatch No. 1005)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 1019 on the Kwantung police rebellion and the resulting threat to the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Tokyo Despatch No. 1019 regarding the open defiance by Kwantung civilian police against being subordinated to the military gendarmerie. Points out that the issue has escalated into a broad clash between civil and military governance, threatening the stability of the Okada Cabinet. Mentions rumors that court circles close to the Throne are dissatisfied with Okada's inability to curb the military and are contemplating replacements such as Ishii, Saito, or Takahashi.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 1019

subfiles.about: Embassy report on the escalating dispute between civilian police and the Kwantung Army Gendarmerie and its potential to cause the collapse of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Details the escalating resistance of 5,000 civilian police in Manchuria to military subordination, including the dispatch of delegates to Tokyo and the suppression of newspapers that published their anti-military manifesto. Explains that the confrontation puts Premier Okada in a dilemma that could force his resignation, as well as prompting General Hishikari's resignation. Reports growing civilian resentment toward army aggrandizement and rumors that imperial advisers are seeking a new prime minister.
subfiles.title: Dispute over Administration in Manchuria and Its Effect on Internal Japanese Politics (Despatch No. 1019)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 1007 (Political Report No. 82) covering the Japanese Cabinet during September 1934.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1007 (Political Report No. 82), dated October 1, 1934, relating to the affairs of the Japanese Cabinet during September 1934. Filed under 894.00 P.R./82 and recorded in decimal file 894.002/254.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/254 (Despatch No. 1007)

subfiles.about: Monthly political report section covering internal political developments, diplomatic service reforms, press retractions, military personnel appointments, and civil aviation expansion in September 1934.
subfiles.summary: Presents Section XII (Internal Political Affairs) of the monthly report for September 1934. Discusses speculation over the Overseas Ministry portfolio, the creation of a Foreign Office Efficiency Committee under Shigemitsu, and the Kokumin Shimbun's forced retraction of corruption allegations against Kwantung police. Further covers the appointment of Generals Araki and Abe to lead grand army maneuvers, impending naval shifts, political party disagreements on rice control, and the program to expand civil aviation as a reserve air force.
subfiles.title: Internal Political Affairs (Japan Monthly Political Report for September 1934)

subfiles.about: Embassy telegram reporting the resignation of Finance Minister Fujii due to ill health and the return of Korekiyo Takahashi to the post.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Minister of Finance Sadanobu Fujii resigned due to poor health, having suffered a physical breakdown during recent Cabinet struggles. Announces that he has been succeeded immediately by former Finance Minister Korekiyo Takahashi.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 261 from Tokyo (Resignation of Finance Minister Fujii)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 1050 (Political Report No. 83) regarding anticipated changes in the Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1050 (Political Report No. 83), dated November 12, 1934, indicating probable changes in the Cabinet resulting from the dissatisfaction of liberals close to the Throne. Filed under 894.00 P.R./83 with cross-reference 894.002/256.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/256 (Despatch No. 1050)

subfiles.about: Monthly political report excerpt discussing political dissatisfaction with the Okada Cabinet, ministerial appointments, and plans for a national policy commission.
subfiles.summary: Presents Section III(a) of the monthly report for October 1934. Notes rumors that Prince Saionji, Count Makino, and other court liberals are dissatisfied with Premier Okada's inability to control the military, floating Ishii, Saito, and Takahashi as prospective successors. Records the appointment of Count Hideo Kodama as Minister for Overseas Affairs and describes plans to create an official advisory commission on national policy.
subfiles.title: Internal Political Affairs (Japan Monthly Political Report for October 1934)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 1074 reporting on the resignation of Fujii and reappointment of Takahashi as Finance Minister.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1074, dated November 30, 1934, which reports the circumstances surrounding the resignation of Sadanobu Fujii as Minister of Finance and the appointment of Korekiyo Takahashi as his successor. Filed under 894.512/26 with cross-reference 894.002/257.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/257 (Despatch No. 1074)

subfiles.about: Embassy report announcing the appointment of General Jiro Minami to succeed General Takashi Hishikari in Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Reports the appointment of General Jiro Minami to the joint posts of Commander of the Kwantung Army, Ambassador to Manchukuo, and administrator of the Kwantung Leased Territory, succeeding General Takashi Hishikari. States that the change in personnel does not reflect a change in policy, but is intended to implement the newly enacted governmental reorganization in Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Japanese Representation in "Manchukuo" (Despatch No. 1078)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 1161 (Political Report No. 86) regarding the proposed national policy study commission.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1161 (Political Report No. 86), dated February 7, 1935, regarding the proposed commission for the study of national policies to serve as an advisory body to the Cabinet. Filed under 894.00 P.R./86 with cross-reference 894.002/259.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/259 (Despatch No. 1161)

subfiles.about: Monthly political report excerpt describing the composition, candidate members, and political controversy surrounding the proposed Cabinet advisory commission.
subfiles.summary: Presents Section (b) of the January 1935 political report regarding the proposed Cabinet advisory commission on national policies. Lists candidate members from political parties, military services, and financial circles, including Makoto Saito, Tatsuo Yamamoto, Korekiyo Takahashi, Kikujiro Ishii, and Keinosuke Goh. Explains the Seiyukai's staunch opposition based on suspicions that the body will form the core of a pro-government political party.
subfiles.title: The Cabinet (Japan Monthly Political Report for January 1935)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Embassy Despatch No. 1332 reporting on the establishment of the Cabinet Deliberative Body and Cabinet Investigation Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Indexes Tokyo Despatch No. 1332, dated May 31, 1935, reporting on the official creation of two new advisory organs subsidiary to the Japanese Cabinet: the Cabinet Deliberative Body and the Cabinet Investigation Bureau. Filed under 894.00/546 with cross-reference 894.002/260.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.002/260 (Despatch No. 1332)

subfiles.about: Embassy report on the formal creation, statutory authority, and appointed membership of the Cabinet Deliberative Body and Cabinet Investigation Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Reports the promulgation of Imperial Ordinance No. 119 establishing the Cabinet Deliberative Body (Naikaku Shingikai) and the Cabinet Investigation Bureau (Naikaku Chosakyoku). Explains their mandates to deliberate and investigate national policies under the Prime Minister. Lists the appointment of Finance Minister Takahashi as vice president and fourteen prominent statesmen, peers, and financiers appointed to the Deliberative Body.
subfiles.title: Cabinet Deliberative Body and Cabinet Investigation Bureau (Despatch No. 1332)
